transcript:
Header: 2026-11-18 20:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair, Marco Ruiz, Jules Park (Redwood) — Samir Patel, Leah Wong, Tom Reeves, Priya Shah (DataLoom)

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off in a sec, Samir, Leah, can you hear us ok?
00:06 Samir Patel: yeah loud and clear, thanks Alex, excited to see — we sent over the doc with our current traffic profile, it's kinda spiky, lots of short chats and some long document summarizations.
00:15 Alex Chen: perfect, that's exactly what we wanted to validate. quick agenda: demo the API, show Console observability, then Priya will run through a high-TPS simulation and talk about streaming/backpressure and timeouts.
00:25 Leah Wong: main constraints for us: 32k token contexts for docs, bursts to 5k TPS for embedding-ish calls, and we need private deployment for PHI. also latency SLO of sub 250ms p50 for short calls.
00:38 Priya Nair: noted. quick clarification: when you say 5k TPS is that sustained or bursts? and are embeddings mixed with generation?
00:45 Tom Reeves: mostly bursts, sustained more like 1k, but spikes hit 4-6k for a few minutes. some generator calls are streaming, yes.
00:52 Alex Chen: ok great. jumping into the API. so our text/generation endpoint supports streaming via chunked HTTP or websocket, you can set max_new_tokens and stream tokens as they come. for long contexts we use prefix/KV cache and sharded attention optimizations on our runtime.
01:08 Priya Nair: (screen share) here's the Console — per-route latency heatmap, token-level cost, and our backpressure metrics. you can see an example where backpressure starts at 250ms queueing and we auto-route to dedicated pool after threshold.
01:27 Leah Wong: pause — in that example when you route, do you switch model variants or just capacity?
01:32 Priya Nair: mostly capacity, we can also fallback to a quantized variant with slightly lower quality to reduce latency. it's configurable in rollout policies.
01:40 Samir Patel: and data residency — for the on-prem case we'd run the private control plane in our VPC, correct? how are keys handled?
01:47 Jules Park: yes, you can run Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane in your VPC. KMS/HSM integration supported, zero-keystore mode optional, audit logs forwarded to your SIEM.
01:58 Priya Shah: Do you have SOC2 and pen test reports?
02:02 Jules Park: we do, I'll share the SOC2 Type II and pen test summary post-call — link will be in the follow-up.
02:08 Marco Ruiz: quick note on cost control: Optimize can recommend batching and quantization profiles per workload; for docs-heavy long-context tasks we usually suggest larger prefix cache TTL and chunking to avoid re-encoding the entire doc on every request.
02:21 Tom Reeves: interesting. on the streaming/backpressure side, what exactly happens when the runtime hits queueing? do you drop connections, do you throttle?
02:29 Priya Nair: good question — we try to avoid dropping. default behavior is to throttle at the router and emit 503 when queue timeout exceeded; we also support graceful degradation: switch to smaller model variant, reduce max_new_tokens, or fall back to cached completions. streaming clients get chunked 'partial' tokens until we close.
02:45 Samir Patel: is there a per-request timeout we can control? we don't want clients hung for minutes.
02:49 Alex Chen: yes, the API exposes request_timeout_ms and stream_timeout_ms, plus you can set per-route policies in the Console. defaults are conservative but we can tune for your case.
02:58 Priya Nair: ok I'm going to run a short simulation — 64k-context model (note: transcription occasionally shows 64k as 6-4-k), sustained 1k TPS, burst to 5k, mixed streaming generation + embeddings. I'll share the terminal.
03:10 Priya Nair: starting load test — watch the metrics, latency distribution, queue depth.
03:23 (beep background)
03:30 Priya Nair: you can already see p95 rising as queues fill; at 3.5k we hit our soft threshold and we start autoscaling dedicated pool. streaming throughput holds but token latency increases.
03:48 Leah Wong: in that trace, what's the CPU/GPU split? are you doing any sequence parallel or kernel fusion?
03:54 Priya Nair: runtime uses optimized kernels and attention fusion where available; for 64k contexts we also shard KV across GPUs to keep GPU memory usable — there's some extra token latency from KV fetch.
04:06 Tom Reeves: what about cold start when fetching huge KV cache? does that blow up latency?
04:10 Priya Nair: cold misses are more expensive; we recommend warming via prefetch or keeping a hot set pinned in dedicated pools. Optimize can suggest pin lists by pattern.
04:19 Samir Patel: our security team will need the network diagram; also are audit logs immutable?
04:24 Jules Park: logs are append-only and can be forwarded to your SIEM; for Private you control retention and immutability via your storage.
04:31 Priya Shah: any known issues with streaming and client libraries? we have a mix of browser and server clients.
04:36 Marco Ruiz: we maintain SDKs with chunked streaming and reconnection logic; transient reconnects are supported — but if the server returns a 503 due to queue timeout clients should retry with backoff or fallback to cached response.
04:48 Priya Nair: back to the load test, I'm going to push to a sustained 5k for 2 minutes to see how backpressure behaves.
05:02 (keyboard clacking)
05:15 Priya Nair: pushing — see small spike, queue depth hits threshold, router starts shedding lower-priority traffic and routes premium traffic to dedicated instances. we logged a few 503s for best-effort jobs.
05:30 Samir Patel: can we set per-API class priorities? e.g., internal critical traffic always gets dedicated lane.
05:35 Alex Chen: yes absolutely — route policies let you map by API key, IP, or header to tiered pools. you can also set SLO enforcement policies.
05:42 Leah Wong: about timeouts — what is the recommended client timeout for streaming vs non-streaming?
05:46 Priya Nair: for streaming we recommend stream_timeout_ms ~ 120000 (2m) but also implement heartbeat/ping; for non-streaming shorter request timeout like 15s for short calls. for long doc summarization you might want 90s or more but combined with prefix cache it's faster.
06:00 Tom Reeves: ok that makes sense. can the Console show per-token cost during the test? we want to understand unit economics under bursts.
06:06 Priya Nair: yes, token-level cost shows up; Optimize can produce cost projections given your workload mix. we'll attach an example spreadsheet.
06:12 Samir Patel: any library/tooling for offline batch processing so we don't overload serving? we have nightly jobs to re-embed docs.
06:17 Marco Ruiz: recommend using Redwood Batch (batch API) or offload to a dedicated batch cluster; it can run large throughput jobs with controlled concurrency.
06:24 Leah Wong: one thing: our infra is behind a strict firewall — for Private on-prem what's the connectivity model?
06:29 Jules Park: Private supports air-gapped installs or VPC peering; for air-gapped we ship an appliance and you can keep control plane on-prem. we'll include deployment options doc.
06:36 Priya Shah: what's the expected SLA for Dedicated? we need 99.9 for tiers.
06:40 Alex Chen: Dedicated has SLA tiers (99.9 and 99.95) depending on capacity commitment. we'll include the SLA table in the follow-up.
06:48 (brief silence, typing)
06:55 Leah Wong: any limitations on model size or quantization with long contexts? we've seen hallucination increase when quantized.
06:59 Priya Nair: yes quantization can affect quality; Optimize recommends mixed strategy: quantize embeddings and use FP for final-generation models, or use model-aware quant profiles. we can run evals on your prompt sets to measure regressions.
07:12 Samir Patel: do you support canary rollouts for model changes? we need to test new checkpoint with 5% traffic first.
07:16 Alex Chen: yes built-in canary and A/B with automatic rollback on errors or quality regressions.
07:22 Tom Reeves: during your stress test did you see any timeouts that led to orphaned streams or memory leaks?
07:28 Priya Nair: we instrument for orphan detection; there were a handful of orphaned streams at extreme loads in our synthetic test but they were reclaimed. we'll include logs in the bench.
07:37 Samir Patel: great. so what's the POC flow? we want on-prem pilot to validate latency and the high-TPS pattern.
07:42 Alex Chen: typical flow: share infra access and traffic profile -> Redwood runs a benchmark -> provision a short Dedicated/Private trial -> run your workload and evals -> sign. we'll draft a statement of work.
07:52 Leah Wong: timeline: we'd like a week-of-11/29 pilot. can you commit to the benchmark results by 11/24?
07:57 Priya Nair: yes we'll run the benchtop and share results.
08:03 Jules Park: I'll send SOC2, network diagrams, and KMS notes after this meeting.
08:07 Alex Chen: ok quick recap and next steps: Alex send pricing and options; Priya run bench; Jules share security docs; Samir confirm pilot contacts. any final q's?
08:17 Samir Patel: none from me, thanks everyone.
08:19 Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with links — I'll put the benchmark spreadsheet, deck, and ticket for pilot in the follow-up.
08:25 (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript has minor transcription noise (e.g., "64k" auto-split). Shared artifacts: deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/deck/edgecases-demo), bench spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/bench/dataloom-20261118), SOC2 doc placeholder (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2).
